attempts.summary: Established a VyOS(node1)-to-OPNsense(node2) site-to-site IPsec tunnel over the transit network, carrying lan-a (10.10.1.0/24, node3) and lan-b (10.10.2.0/24, node4) so node3 and node4 reach each other by private address with traffic encrypted on the wire. Discovered the physical wiring empirically (node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 = transit; node1 eth2<->node3 eth1 = lan-a; node2 vtnet2<->node4 eth1 = lan-b), addressed all links, configured VyOS IKEv2/ESP site-to-site peer with PSK auth, configured OPNsense's swanctl-based IPsec (Connections/locals/remotes/children plus the legacy ipsec.enable flag and dynamic enc0 interface registration) plus firewall pass rules for IKE/ESP and the enc0 pseudo-interface, added static routes on the RHEL7 leaf nodes, and validated bidirectional encrypted ping traffic (ESP frames observed on the transit wire, byte counters incrementing on both IPsec SAs). Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes, confirming changed boot identity (boot_id/boottime) and full post-restart recovery of interfaces, the IPsec tunnel (auto-reconnected), firewall rules, and end-to-end node3<->node4 connectivity after each restart.
